heroHeadline: Ukraine's Largest-Ever Drone Attack Hits Moscow Refinery as Forces Advance in Donetsk
heroSubtitle: Ukraine carried out its largest-ever combined drone/missile strike on a Moscow Oblast oil refinery and logistics facility overnight September 19-20, on the final day of Russia's State Duma elections, killing 3 and injuring 20; the same day, Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps liberated Shandryholove and Derylove and took full control of Drobysheve in Operation Vivaldi's second phase in Donetsk Oblast, with cumulative Russian losses in the operation exceeding 3,000 personnel. Russia continued striking civilian areas: overnight drone attacks on Kyiv Oblast's Fastiv district killed a mother and her two 3-year-old children and, separately, another girl died in hospital (September 20), while a drone strike near an apartment building in Sumy killed a woman and injured her husband (September 21). Separately, the UN documented 1,004 verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence since 2022, 89% attributed to Russian forces (September 18), and the US State Department approved a $2.7 billion air-defense sale to Ukraine (September 19). Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,519,650 by September 21, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
